company_name: キリンホールディングス
investment_thesis: Kirin combines a mature domestic beer business with health science and overseas beverage assets, and the latest year restored the operating margin to the top of its four-year range; the shares trade at {per} earnings and {pb} book.
The cost of debt in this model is the realised rate from the filings rather than an assumed spread, which matters because leverage sits between the domestic beverage peers and the more geared names.
At {price} the market is not paying for the margin recovery to hold; a base case that mean-reverts only partway supports {target_price}, or {upside_pct} from here.
key_risks: The health-science expansion has absorbed capital without yet delivering peer-level returns, and a write-down there would take earnings back toward the trough case rather than the {per} implied by {price}.
Domestic beer volumes decline structurally, so modelled growth relies on overseas assets whose currencies are not hedged in the {wacc} used here.
The latest-year margin is the best in the observation window; if it proves to be a peak rather than a new level, the base case overstates the path behind {target_price}.
